title: Edge GPU queueing and backfill review — July 16 2027
content:
Purpose:
Quick sync notes from the ad-hoc weekly on edge GPU queueing pressure and the newly deployed backfill scheduler. Goal: capture observed behavior, immediate mitigations, action items for next week, and a lightweight hypothesis list for longer-term fixes.

Attendees:
- Marina Patel (note-taker)
- Ethan Kim (edge-fleet lead)
- Sofia Alvarez (serving runtime)
- Jonah Reed (SRE)
- Priya Iyer (capacity planning)
- Casual drop-ins: Ops rotation (Anand), Solutions eng (Tasha)

Summary / TL;DR:
- After the July 12 backfill scheduler change (PR in linked artifacts), we saw improved utilization on small-edge clusters but an unexpected queue spike for 2-4 minute inference jobs during regional spikes (US-Central + APAC-1) from July 14–16.
- Root-cause hypothesis: backfill policy combined with continuous-batching heuristics is causing long-lived prefix reservations that block mid-tail short jobs; scheduler retries are amplifying queue churn.
- Immediate mitigation (rolled out 07-15 04:30 UTC): limit prefix-reservation lifetime to 18s on edge nodes and disable aggressive retry window. Reduced median queue depth from ~9 -> ~4 in US-Central; tail latency still elevated.

Metrics observed (sampling window 2027-07-14 -> 2027-07-16):
- Edge cluster US-Central:
  - average queue depth pre-change: 8.9
  - average queue depth post-change: 4.1
  - p95 wait time pre-change: 2.8s -> post-change: 1.6s
  - p99 wait time pre-change: 23s -> post-change: 14s
- APAC-1 showed similar queue depth drop but p99 only moved 30% (from 18s -> 12.5s).
- Backfill utilization improved by ~6% cluster-wide (measured as % idle-GPU time reclaimed).

Observed unusual behaviors / notes:
1) Multi-workload collision: when two high-priority streams (hosted-api burst + dedicated prewarm) enter region, the backfill reservation grabs contiguous slots and holds them for prefix caching, starving short on-demand requests.
2) Retry storms: some clients (internal stress test harness) retry at 100ms intervals on 429/503, producing a feedback loop that increases short-job queueing.
3) Sequence-length variance: models with long KV caches are occupying slots longer than expected; our current heuristics underweight KV length in reservation scoring.
4) Edge provisioning jitter: node churn (kube evictions) increases scheduling churn; backfill currently treats ephemeral node loss as a soft failure and retries aggressively rather than redistributing reservations.

Decisions made in meeting:
- Short term: leave prefix-reservation lifetime at 18s and keep aggressive retry disabled for the remainder of the week. If p99 does not improve by Friday, revert to previous scheduler and run controlled A/B. (Owner: Ethan)
- Medium term: update reservation scoring to include KV-cache-weight and model-seq-length buckets. Prototype scoring update in canary region next sprint. (Owner: Sofia + Jonah)
- Observability: add a backfill-reservation timeline trace to Console, showing reservation create/extend/evict events at token-level granularity. Target: dashboard by 2027-07-27. (Owner: Marina + Observability)

Action items (short form):
- Ethan: run focused chaos test for node-eviction + backfill in staging (INFRA-842). Due 2027-07-20.
- Sofia: open runtime change RFC capturing KV-cache weight heuristic; include microbench results for two models (gpt-small-8k, rw-large-16k). Due 2027-07-22.
- Jonah: instrument retry-source tagging in request logs and ship a filter to drop known test harness patterns from production metrics. Due 2027-07-19.
- Priya: recalc regional capacity buffer for APAC-1 and propose small reserve (+5%) for on-demand lane. Due 2027-07-21.
- Marina: add a short postmortem-lite note with timeline and link it into the incident playbook. Due 2027-07-18.

Open hypotheses (for later investigation):
- H1: Our continuous-batching heuristic assumes uniform request length; adding a distribution-aware estimator will reduce prefix reservation durations by ~20%.
- H2: Node churn causes reservation fragmentation; a soft-handshake protocol for reservation transfer may reduce scheduler thrash.
- H3: Some long-p99 tail sources are internal test harnesses; adding client-id backpressure in the routing tier will blunt retry storms without impacting real customers.

Risk assessment and rollback plan:
- Risk: Changing reservation scoring could reduce reclaimed utilization, increasing cost. Mitigation: run scoring change behind feature flag + percent rollout, monitor unit-cost-per-token and fallback to previous policy after 30m if cost crosses threshold.
- Rollback: scheduler config can be reverted cluster-wide in under 6 minutes (documented runbook). If rollback fails, fallback is to disable backfill entirely and rely on static bin-packing (manual operation, 45–90m).

Notes from debugging session (details):
- Captured a 12-minute trace where a single reservation was extended 18 times due to batching window extension; the job holding the reservation stalled at model load due to a transient NVMe issue. Root cause here is cascading: storage glitch -> model load stalls -> reservation retained -> short job queue grows. Storage team engaged for further analysis.
- We saw a pattern where request retries include stale route-tokens; adding a TTL to route cookies reduced duplicates in staging.

Communication plan:
- Internal: send a short status update to #infra-ops and #edge-fleet after action items are created. Marina will draft the note.
- External (customers): no external incidents; only advise dedicated capacity customers of potential short tail latency increases in APAC-1; Solutions Eng will curate a short note if needed.

Appendix: quick runbook snippets (for on-call)
- Immediate steps when queue depth > 12 for > 10m:
  1) Identify dominant reservation owners via /observability/reservations API.
  2) Temporarily set reservation-lifetime = 6s for affected region.
  3) Throttle internal retrying clients by injecting 429 with Retry-After 5s at edge-router.
  4) Notify SRE rotation and escalate to Ethan if metrics don't drop in 10m.

- Helpful Jira links and PRs (see linked_artifacts).

Next meeting:
- Quick checkpoint Tuesday 2027-07-19 09:00 UTC (15m) to review action-item status and p99 trend. Full follow-up on 2027-07-23 (weekly sync).

Notes to self (informal):
- Try to capture a short gif of reservation timeline — very helpful for postmortem slides.
- Keep an eye on dedicated prewarm schedule; it's a major confounder for edge microbursts.
- Consider adding an internal flag to simulate KV-heavy model to stress-test reservation scoring.

End of notes.
